verdict: MRVL +32% on Jensen Huang 'next trillion' endorsement at Computex; AVGO AI beats but Q3 guide below buy-side — AI thesis intact, market priced for perfection.
body_md:
## Fresh developments (last 24-72h)

**MRVL +32% (Jun 2) + ~10% extended (Jun 3 pre-market).** Jensen Huang called Marvell Technology "the next trillion-dollar company" at Computex on stage with CEO Matt Murphy, citing MRVL's networking/connectivity chips as essential to distributed AI compute across thousands of connected chips. Stifel raised PT to $321. Baseline must-catch scenario made literal: NVIDIA CEO explicitly names and endorses a watchlist name.

**AVGO Q2 FY2026 (reported Jun 3): AI beat, software miss, no guide raise.** AI semiconductor revenue $10.8B (+143% YoY, above forecast). Total revenue $22.19B vs $22.27B consensus; software segment $7.18B vs $7.32B est. Q3 AI guide: $16B — exceptional in absolute terms but below aggressive buy-side models (~$17.2B). FY2027 $100B+ AI outlook reiterated without upward revision. Stock -3% to -12.6% on day. Sector contagion: MU -3.3%, NVDA/AMD softer.

**DRAM Q2 pricing decelerating: +58-63% QoQ** (vs Q1's +90-95%). NAND +70-75% QoQ. HBM remains pre-committed and sold out through 2026. Pace of gains is slowing — directionally consistent with baseline correction-risk flag.

**Section 232 solar tariff ruling still pending.** Decision expected "end of May" per prior guidance; as of Jun 5 no announcement. FSLR remains elevated on anticipation. CdTe technology insulates First Solar from polysilicon exposure.

**Signals 4 & 5 (AMD/Optical): No fresh 24-72h catalysts.** AMD MI400/Helios on track for Q3 2026 per prior guidance. InP shortage and 18+ month equipment lead times persist; COHR 6-inch ramp ongoing.

**HIVE/BUZZ:** $30M AI cloud contracts signed Feb 2026 (not fresh); watch Q4 2026 $140M ARR target and BTC price correlation.

---

| Name | Move | Catalyst |
|------|------|----------|
| MRVL | +32% Jun 2 + extended | Jensen Huang "next trillion-dollar company" at Computex |
| AVGO | -3% to -12.6% Jun 3-4 | Software miss; Q3 AI guide $16B < buy-side ~$17.2B |
| MU | -3.3% | AVGO sector contagion |
| FSLR | Elevated, no fresh move | Section 232 tariff decision imminent |

---

## Context vs baseline

MRVL move is the baseline's "NVIDIA naming a watchlist name" trigger executed perfectly. AVGO AI trajectory ($10.8B Q2 → $16B Q3 → $100B+ FY2027) remains on-thesis, but lack of upward revision is the first sign the market is pricing perfection — any soft data point lands hard. DRAM Q2 deceleration from Q1 peak (+95% → +63%) is an early datapoint supporting the baseline's post-2026 correction-risk flag; HBM all-three-supplier capacity expansion is on track for late-2026.

---

## Signals flashing

| Signal | Direction | Bull/Bear |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| DRAM Q2 pricing | Decelerating from Q1 peak | Mild bear vs Q1 |
| HBM4 ramp (3 suppliers) | Expanding supply late-2026 | Bear for post-2026 pricing |
| Hyperscaler capex | $650-700B, no guide-downs | Bull |
| NVDA → MRVL endorsement | Explicit public naming | Strongly bull |
| AVGO AI Q3 guide | $16B (no raise vs $100B+ path) | Mixed |
| Solar Section 232 | Ruling imminent | Bull for FSLR if enacted |
| Optical InP shortage | Persists; COHR ramp in progress | Bull COHR/LITE near-term |

---

## Most important development

**MRVL +32% on Jensen Huang's "next trillion-dollar company" endorsement at Computex (Jun 2)** is the week's defining event — the baseline's must-catch scenario executed in real time. Simultaneously, AVGO's $16B Q3 AI guide (vs buy-side ~$17.2B) injects the first note of caution: AI capex demand is enormous and growing, but the market is priced for upward revisions, not reiterations.
